sec: HCV structure, lipoviral particle, genome, genes and DAA suffixes, genotypes, transmission

items.q: Fill up (Structure): '______ sense RNA virus : ______ (Family), ______ (Sub family).'
items.exp: '+ve sense RNA virus : Flaviviridae (Family), Hepaciviridae (Sub family)'. (Book p1045)

items.q: How does the page describe the HCV virion?
opts: A lipoviral particle bound to VLDL / LDL
items.exp: 'Virion (lipo viral particle) : Bound to VLDL / LDL — causes Steatosis'. (Book p1045)

items.q: Which mechanism does this page give for steatosis in chronic hepatitis C?
opts: The lipoviral particle is bound to VLDL / LDL
items.exp: 'Virion (lipo viral particle) : Bound to VLDL/LDL → causes Steatosis'. (Book p1045)

items.q: Judge the steatosis note: I Hepatitis A, B and D are listed as not causing steatosis. II HCV causes steatosis through its lipoviral particle.
items.exp: 'Hepatitis A, B, D & E do not cause steatosis' follows the lipoviral-particle note. (Book p1045)

items.q: Genome length and coding capacity printed for HCV?
opts: 9.7 kb, coding for about 3,000 amino acids as a polyprotein
3.2 kb, coding for about 300 amino acids
9.7 kb, coding for four separate structural proteins only
1.7 kb, coding for about 900 amino acids
items.exp: 'Length : 9.7 kb — codes for ~3000 amino acid polyprotein'. (Book p1045)

items.q: Which host enzyme is printed as cleaving the structural from the non-structural genes?
items.exp: 'Structural genes / Non-structural genes' are separated by 'host signal peptidase'. (Book p1045)

items.q: DAA drug-name suffixes — match — 1) NS3 2) NS5A 3) NS5B … A) -asvir B) -buvir C) -previr
items.exp: 'NS3 (-) : Previr; NS5A (-) : Asvir; NS5B (-) : buvir' under 'New Directly Acting Antivirals (DAAs)'. (Book p1045)

items.q: How many HCV genotypes does the page print, and which one is commonest in India?
items.exp: '7 genotypes : Genotype 1 : m/c (world); Genotype 3 : m/c (India)'. (Book p1045)

items.q: Judge the genotype note: I Genotype 1 is the commonest worldwide. II Genotype 3, commonest in India, carries the worst prognosis and is linked to cirrhosis and HCC.
items.exp: 'Genotype 1 : m/c (world)'; 'Genotype 3 : m/c (India) — worst prognosis'; 'Note : Associated with Cirrhosis / Hepatocellular carcinoma'. (Book p1045)

items.q: The note 'Hepatitis A, B, D & E do not cause steatosis' is printed next to the description of which virus?
items.exp: The note follows the HCV lipoviral-particle line that explains steatosis. (Book p1045)

items.q: Transmission — match the route to the printed risk — 1) Transfusion 2) IV drug users 3) Sexual modes … A) 40 – 90% B) Negligible C) 1 in 10,00,000
Which group is printed as the commonest setting (m/c in) for HCV infection?
What does the page print for post-exposure prophylaxis against HCV?
Which is NOT one of the printed transmission headings for HCV?
items.exp: Printed headings: Percutaneous, Transfusion, Perinatal / Breast feeding, Sexual modes, IV drug users. (Book p1045)

items.q: Perinatal / breast-feeding transmission of HCV is printed in which risk band?
opts: A low single-digit percentage — far below the 40 – 90% seen in IV drug users
40 – 90%, the same as IV drug users
Negligible, the same as sexual transmission
items.exp: Perinatal / breast feeding is printed in the single-digit percent range, against 40-90% for IV drug users, negligible for sexual exposure and 1 in 10,00,000 for transfusion. (Book p1045)
